body.p: After you stage the files that you want to include, enter a commit message in the Commit message area and click Commit to save the staged changes to your local repository. You can also reuse a previous commit message.

The toolbar above the Commit message area includes options that affect the commit:
Generate commit message using AI - Creates a draft commit message based on the staged changes.
Amend last commit - Updates the most recent local commit.
Automatically push changes to remote when committing - Pushes after the commit.
You can customize how AI generates commit messages from the Git Client AI preferences page.

ul.li: If your environment is configured for commit signing, you can sign commits using SSH or GPG keys.

GPG support in JGit, the Java library used for Git operations, honors the GNUPGHOME environment variable. If this variable is set to a valid directory path, that directory is used as the GPG home directory where the keys are stored. If GNUPGHOME is not set, JGit defaults to %APPDATA%\gnupg on Windows and ~/.gnupg on other operating systems. Alternatively, you can set the jgit.gpg.home Java system property, which takes precedence over GNUPGHOME if both are set.
